page: OVHcloud r3-64 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Storage is provided via a local 200 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance runs on the KVM hypervisor and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the r3-64 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 3078.58 in stress-ng tests, which places it in the top 25% of tested instances. Its memory subsystem also shows strong capabilities, with a PassMark memory score of 2964.73 and a large-block write bandwidth of 101.05 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance and read-only memory bandwidth fall within the average range, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 24583.04 and large-block read bandwidth reaching 172.7 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform at average levels, with Redis handling 20.07 million operations per second.

The hardware configuration presents a clear tradeoff: the absence of hyperthreading limits parallel thread density but ensures that each vCPU has dedicated physical execution resources without resource contention. This dedicated CPU allocation, combined with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and local NVMe storage, offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive network throughput. The r3-64 is suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, Redis caching layers, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
